messages:
kate.dev: quick sync — running into an edge with the token-tagging rollout and quota/routing. some requests end up on default pool even though token has project=payment tag. can we decide authoritative routing order?

sam_platform: repro + logs? is it happening for all models or a specific path?

kate.dev: repro attached, happens on generation path when request size > 1k tokens (rare). header looks like: `Authorization: Bearer <tk>` and we add `X-RW-Token-Tags: project=payment;env=prod`

kate.dev: logs: 
```
AuthService: introspect -> claims {org: org-123, project: null}
Routing: found tag project=payment on token metadata
Router: chosen pool = default-gpu-1 (confusing)
```

mike_infra: hmm, router prefers claims.project over token tags today. token-tags were meant as a hint only. we didn't make them authoritative because of spoof risk.

irina_prodsec: exact concern — user-mutable token metadata is risky. do we verify tags are server-signed? if not, we should never trust them for quota/routing.

kate.dev: token-tags are stored at mint time and signed in token metadata by Auth (jwt claim token_tags with signature). so they are signed, but the router code path currently skips them for long requests because we short-circuit on claim cache.

sam_platform: ok that sounds like an implementation bug then. two questions: 1) do we want token-tags to override project claim? 2) what metric/telemetry to add to catch mismatches?

mike_infra: proposal: routing precedence = [explicit project claim, token_tags.project, org fallback]. but we should add an allowlist: only certain tags (project, tenant) are valid for routing.

irina_prodsec: agree on allowlist + require tokens to have 'iss' = auth.redwood and not be client-provided. also audit log every time token_tags != claims.project for 30d.

ops_john: for dashboards: can we surface a metric like `auth.routing.tag_mismatch_count` and `auth.routing.used_token_tag` with labels {pool, model, org, project_tag, claim_project}? needs to be cheap.

kate.dev: yep can emit counters + sample a few traces. example metrics: 
```
counter: auth_routing_tag_mismatch_total{pool="default-gpu-1", model="rw-2b", org="org-123", token_tag="payment", claim_project=""} 1
gauge: auth_routing_last_time_tag_used{project_tag="payment"} 1700000000
```

sam_platform: rollout plan: 1) hotfix router to consider signed token_tags, behind flag `auth.token_tag.routing` 2) enable canary 5% infra for a few hours, monitor mismatch metric 3) 25% -> 100% with rollback if error rate or latency spike.

mike_infra: impl notes: router change is tiny but needs introspect to return token_tags in cached entry. cache key needs to include token_tag signature version so cache invalidation works.

irina_prodsec: add an audit event `auth.token_tag.routing_decision` with fields (caller, token_id, used_tag, used_claim, decision) and wire to long-retention audit cluster.

ops_john: console UX — add a column in tokens table `routing_tag` and a toggle to mark if token tag is allowed for routing. also show metric link for `tag_mismatch` on project page.

kate.dev: I'll draft the PR + console mock. Leaving the flag default off. anyone want to own the canary play?

sam_platform: I'll own canary monitoring. will add dashboards and alert if `auth.routing.tag_mismatch_rate > 0.01` or if p95 latency increases > 200ms.

mike_infra: I'll do the router + cache change.

irina_prodsec: I'll write the audit schema and review PR.

kate.dev: sweet. I'll post the PR number when ready. thanks. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: feature-flag `auth.token_tag.routing` set to 5% for canary (ids: ff-9876)
